tinycc 0.9.28rc, LGPL-2.1 (see COPYING). Vendored from
https://repo.or.cz/tinycc.git @ 64552b3faa39ee7948a9ea21bfcc11045b90c70d
(the last tag, release_0_9_27, is from 2017 and HEAD is ~1400 commits past it,
so a commit is the only usable pin). `src/` holds the subset an x86_64 build
touches, on Linux and on Windows -- the nine core .c files, their headers, the
x86_64 backend, `lib/`, `include/`, `Makefile`, `configure`, `conftest.c`, and
for Windows (PE) `tccpe.c`, `win32/include/` (with `winapi/`), the startup and
helper sources of `win32/lib/` and `win32/tcc-win32.txt` -- with no other
backend, no tests, no examples and no docs. Upstream's `win32/lib/*.def` import
lists are not vendored: a Windows build generates its own from the system's
DLLs with tcc's `-impdef`. Built by upstream's own Makefile from a staged copy
under `out/`; see the Makefile `out/tcc` rule.

LGPL-2.1 in this dual MIT/Apache tree means **dlopen only, never static-link**:
static linking is what triggers LGPL section 6's relink obligation. `make
static-tcc-guard` enforces it -- no driver binary may define `tcc_new`.

## Local patches

The tree is the pinned upstream except for these changes, each marked
`zerolang local patch` where it is made. All of them are for Windows (PE); the
Linux build is upstream's.

- **The UCRT, not msvcrt.dll.** Every other Windows compiler links the
  Universal CRT (ucrtbase.dll); upstream tcc links msvcrt.dll, whose printf
  writes `1e+018` and `1.#INF`, rounds exactly-halfway values the other way,
  and which has no `fma` or `nearbyint`. A program built by tcc must behave as
  one built by gcc or cl, so:
  - `tccpe.c`: the default CRT library is `ucrtbase`.
  - `win32/include/_ucrt.h` (new), included last from `_mingw.h`: FILE is
    opaque and the standard streams are `__acrt_iob_func(0..2)`; `__argc`,
    `__argv`, `_environ`, `_pgmptr`, `_fmode`, `MB_CUR_MAX` and `_pctype` go
    through the UCRT's accessors; `_HUGE` is a constant; errno gains the POSIX
    values the UCRT defines (100-140); `rand_s` is declared. Each msvcrt form
    in the headers below is behind an `#ifndef` of the same name, so defining
    the UCRT form first selects it.
  - `win32/lib/ucrt.c` (new, in libtcc1.a via `lib/Makefile`): the functions
    the UCRT provides only as header inlines -- the printf and scanf families
    (narrow and wide, over `__stdio_common_*`, with C99 `snprintf` and the
    IEEE rounding of halfway values), `time`/`localtime`/`gmtime`/`mktime`/
    `ctime`/`difftime` (over the `_*64` forms) and `atexit`. The locale (`_l`),
    positional (`_p`), secure (`_s`) and console (`_c`) printf variants are
    not provided.
  - `win32/include/stdio.h`, `wchar.h`: `vsnprintf` and `vsnwprintf` are
    declarations (libtcc1.a's), not inlines over msvcrt's `_vsnprintf`.
  - `win32/lib/crt1.c`, `wincrt1.c`: the UCRT's startup calls
    (`_configure_narrow_argv`/`_configure_wide_argv`,
    `_initialize_*_environment`, `_set_app_type`, `_seh_filter_exe`) in place
    of msvcrt's `__getmainargs`, `__set_app_type` and `_XcptFilter`.
- **Vista-and-later declarations** this reduced winapi lacks, for zerolang's
  runtime: SRW locks, condition variables, `InitOnceExecuteOnce`,
  `SetThreadDescription`, `STARTUPINFOEXW` and the proc-thread attribute list,
  `GetActiveProcessorCount`, `GetTickCount64`, `GetFileInformationByHandleEx`
  with `FILE_BASIC_INFO`/`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TAG_INFO`, `CreateSymbolicLinkW`,
  `FindExInfoBasic`, `FIND_FIRST_EX_LARGE_FETCH` (`winapi/winbase.h`);
  `IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK` (`winnt.h`); `ERROR_DIRECTORY_NOT_SUPPORTED`
  (`winerror.h`); `WSA_FLAG_NO_HANDLE_INHERIT` (`winsock2.h`); and the new
  `winapi/tlhelp32.h` (process snapshots) and `winapi/winioctl.h`
  (`FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT`).
- **The x64 multiply and shift intrinsics** `winapi/winnt.h` declares and
  nothing defined (`__umulh`, `__mulh`, `_umul128`, `_mul128`,
  `__shiftleft128`, `__shiftright128`): `win32/lib/winex.c` defines them in
  plain C, so a program using one (SQLite on `_WIN64`) links.
- **`fabs` of -0.0** (an upstream bug):
  `win32/include/tcc/tcc_libm.h` overrides `fabs`/`fabsf`/`fabsl` as
  `x < 0 ? -x : x`, which leaves -0.0 negative; they clear the sign bit.

The import lists (`.def`) a Windows tcc links through are generated by the
built tcc's `-impdef` from the system's own DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, shell32,
ws2_32, ucrtbase, user32, gdi32): see the Makefile.

## Regenerating `config/<os>-<arch>/`

`config.h` and `config.mak` are configure output, not upstream sources. From a
checkout at the pinned commit:

    ./configure --tccdir=/usr/local/lib/tcc
    grep -v '^#define CONFIG_OS_RELEASE' config.h > config/<os>-<arch>/config.h
    cp config.mak config/<os>-<arch>/config.mak

`--tccdir` is a placeholder: nothing reads it, because every invocation passes
`-B <dir>` (driver) or `tcc_set_lib_path` (libtcc), which is the only way tcc
can find `libtcc1.a` and `include/` in a relocatable tree. `CONFIG_OS_RELEASE`
is dropped because configure bakes in the build machine's kernel release; it is
read only by the BSD note-section path in `tccelf.c`, dead on Linux.

The checked-in config targets glibc multiarch: configure probes
`/usr/lib/<triplet>/crti.o` and settles on `x86_64-linux-gnu`. A host laid out
differently (`/usr/lib64`, and so on) needs its own `config/<os>-<arch>/`
generated by the commands above and selected with `make TCC_TRIPLE=<os>-<arch>`.
